description: This course covers propositional logic; Boolean algebra; set theory; relations and functions; graph theory; combinatorics; recurrence relations; and discrete probability. Topics include logical connectives, truth tables, normal forms, and logical equivalence; Boolean operations, De Morgan's laws, and Boolean circuits; set operations, Venn diagrams, and Cartesian products; relations, equivalence classes, and partial orders; graph representations, traversal algorithms like DFS and BFS, and shortest path algorithms like Dijkstra's; combinatorics including permutations, combinations, and the binomial theorem; recurrence relations and their solutions using characteristic equations; and discrete probability distributions like Bernoulli and binomial. The course emphasizes applications in computer science, including formal verification, circuit design, algorithm analysis, and data structures.

clos.text: Define logical connectives and construct truth tables for compound propositions.
Describe set operations and apply them to solve problems involving set membership and cardinality.
Explain graph theory concepts and implement graph traversal algorithms such as DFS and BFS.
Apply combinatorial principles to calculate permutations, combinations, and binomial coefficients.
Implement algorithms for solving recurrence relations and analyze their time complexity.

topics: Propositional Logic: Logical Connectives and Truth Tables
Boolean Algebra: Laws, Theorems, and Circuit Simplification
Set Theory: Set Operations and Venn Diagrams
Relations and Functions: Properties and Applications
Graph Theory: Basic Concepts and Representations
Graph Traversal Algorithms: DFS and BFS Implementation
Shortest Path Algorithms: Dijkstra's and Floyd-Warshall
Discrete Probability: Basic Concepts and Distributions
Probability Applications: Conditional and Bayes' Theorem
Advanced Topics: Random Variables and Expectation
